outer_face.count_source: The west-edge aerial crop includes both return corners, canopy endpoints and all eight ordinary pairs. On the right of the 2024 April oblique photograph (image 26), four pairs end at the far corner. Windmemories February 2026 and November 2025 frontal photographs resolve the individual rings and the central opening separately.
outer_face.aerial_counting_xy: On the 1100x145 aerial-west-edge work crop, the approximate x coordinates of the 18 vertical ring axes at y=79, left to right, are 94,147; 200,252; 313,360; 421,474; 546,574 (central); 650,700; 755,811; 867,921; 981,1039. Read the wide equally spaced piers as boundaries, the narrow intermediate cap as the centre of a pair. Slant is appreciable at the ends; these are axis identifiers, not spacing measurements.
outer_face.position_of_ordinary_panel: Immediately to the image right of the central projecting body, the first upright panel in the first pair. Across the same wide bay is a second equivalent narrow panel.
outer_face.central_treatment: Two continuous vertical stacks against one wider rectangular pier, no side cell matrices. One narrow inset field of diagonal slats flanks the paired stacks at each outside edge. The head extends higher than the normal tooth band, with deep layered central cap.
outer_face.ordinary_crown: Both panels share one long zigzag/triangular shallow relief band and continuous lower drip. A stepped rectangular capital above the narrow central pier projects through the band. The full structural pier is broader and extends uninterrupted above the paired field.
outer_face.side_openings: In each normal panel a 2-column × 24-row rectangle field runs down each side; each circular module corresponds to two side rectangles vertically. The half-pitch horizontal member ends at each inner side post. Glass/mullions visible beyond are separate from these opening edges.

ordinary_cross_section.unit: D = outside diameter of a normal ring in its front plane, not the clear glazed opening. Relative values are estimates.
ordinary_cross_section.links: Full-width heavy upper and lower rails continue between each ring and the two side lattices. Individual circles have cardinal contacts with rails and side jambs. There is no half-pitch bar through an opening, no alternating stagger and no interlaced circle arcs; small triangular ports remain at the four corners of the circular field.
ordinary_cross_section.front_measure_source: 1800×1200 Windmemories frame; inspection crop [1100,473,1240,622] enlarged exactly 4× for edge reading. Three consecutive circles and both full- and half-pitch rails are visible.

source_pixels_for_depth.vertical_scan: Front face changing from light grey at y517 through neutral grey at 519 to dark underside at 520. Rear pale sky/glazing starts at 525–526. A similar offset occurs on the adjacent side rectangular holes.

ordinary_cross_section.depth_interpretation: Recess is directly visible in multiple apertures and from the reverse. EXIF gives a 24 mm full-frame lens; with 1800 px image width, f≈1200 px for an uncropped full frame. Two separated upright court posts put the vertical VP far above the top of frame; estimates use a normal VP roughly at [900,950–1060]. For a hole near [1155,535], a 4–6 px vertical front/back edge offset implies about 0.21–0.42 D before accounting for a possible separate glazing/lip offset. For a display model use 0.27 D as a nominal recess and retain this interval; one photograph cannot separate a back bevel from glazing gap.
ordinary_cross_section.depth_status: photographic estimate, lower confidence; no section drawing, rear glass clearance, tilt or absolute depth confirmed
ordinary_cross_section.inside_check: Han Lei 2010 image, original 1066×1600. At y757 inside side apertures span x107–204,247–350,776–853,898–994. At y806 the side matrix is blocked by its half-pitch rail while central light remains x429–493 and 579–693 either side of the distant chimney. At y627 the full-width divider blocks across. This separates foreground concrete from the chimney or a glass reflection.

period.notice: 1933 municipal Gazette, item 4410, stated the new Municipal Abattoir in Sawgin Road had begun operation.
period.annual_quote: The removal of all the activities to the new Abattoir was completed on January 24
period.scope: The quoted transfer belongs to the report for 1934. These sources date commissioning of the building. The oldest inspected laboratory-quality image for this grille is the 2010 photograph; no identified original as-built sheet or dated completion photograph proves the surviving frame material or all the ring profiles as originally built.
